newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla., official drops charter change plan.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla., official drops charter change plan.

text.p: A Dade County, Fla., commissioner has abandoned an attempt to change the county charter so that suburban residents could vote on a proposal to abolish the City of Miami.

Commissioner Pedro Reboredo gave up the idea after discsussions with other commissioners on Friday failed to garner the needed support. At least nine of the 13 commissioners would have had to approve the change in order to put the charter amendment before voters.

Under the current charter, only City of Miami residents can vote on the proposal to abolish the city. If Miami is dissolved, which recent polls suggest is unlikely, the city would be absorbed by Dade County government.
Reboredo had wanted to extend voting rights to residents of unincorporated areas, who could be affected because their services are provided by the county.
But other commissioners said changing the charter would give the incorrect impression they support the effort the abolish Miami.

Miami residents angry over the city's recent corruption and finance scandals collected enough petition signatures to force a vote on the proposal to dissolve the city. The referendum must held before August but no date has been set.
